MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Possible cystic fibrosis, infertility investigation

TEST PERFORMED
Cystic Fibrosis Common Mutation Panel

METHODOLOGY
Targeted mutation analysis was performed for the following common CFTR gene mutations:
- c.1521_1523delCTT (p.Phe508del, delta F508)
- c.1652G>A (p.Gly551Asp, G551D)
- c.1657C>T (p.Arg553X, R553X)
- c.1624G>T (p.Gly542X, G542X)
- c.350G>A (p.Arg117His, R117H)

This assay would also detect c.1519_1521delATC (p.Ile507del, delta I507) if present.

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and analyzed using allele-specific PCR followed by capillary electrophoresis.

RESULTS
1. No pathogenic variants detected in the CFTR gene for the mutations tested
2. Genotype: Negative for all tested mutations

INTERPRETATION
This patient does not carry any of the common cystic fibrosis mutations included in this panel. These results reduce but do not eliminate the possibility of being a CF carrier, as this panel detects approximately 85-90% of CF mutations in individuals of Northern European descent.

LIMITATIONS
- This test only screens for specific known mutations and does not sequence the entire CFTR gene
- Rare or population-specific mutations would not be detected
- Detection rate varies by ethnicity
- Does not detect large deletions/duplications or intronic variants

CLINICAL CORRELATION
Negative results for common CF mutations reduce carrier risk. In the context of infertility investigation, other causes should be considered. If clinical suspicion for CF remains high, comprehensive CFTR gene sequencing may be warranted.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
